annotations.title: Search Atlas Nodes, Decisions, and Terms

description: Find Atlas entries by topic when you hold no id; an id you already hold can be read directly. Searches Nodes (patterns, concepts, examples) and Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); kind narrows it to one Node kind, Decisions, or glossary terms. Node discovery preserves leading lexical matches and adds related entries with task vocabulary, using references in either direction. Related candidates explain their connection; direct matches have no via. Empty listings and exact id/title lookups stay lexical. Returns ranked ids with Hooks (one-line summaries; a term's is its whole definition), paged with a cursor. A miss is an empty page; invalid arguments are refused as invalid_argument.

bound.description: How many ranked candidates this call returns; raise it to compare more matches at once, and continue past it with cursor.

cursor.description: scope.next_cursor from a prior atlas_orient page; repeat the same other arguments.

expected_revision.description: Pins this call to the Release (published edition) a prior payload named in 'coherence'; refused as 'revision_changed' if the active Release has changed. Omit for the active Release.

kind.description: Narrows the search to one Node kind, to Decision records, or to glossary terms. Omit it to search every Node kind plus Roadmap entries (announced, unpublished); setting it leaves Roadmap entries out.

examples: keep bulky context out of the window

query.description: A topic or question in ordinary design vocabulary. Lexical matches use canonical ids, titles, Hooks, claims, then Section headings and bodies, with rarer words weighing more; a word of four or more characters also matches longer tokens it begins. Section text supplies direct candidates only when no subject matches an identity field. Node discovery also includes neighbors matching query terms through references in either direction; via explains the connection, and total counts the candidates. kind='decision' searches Decision ids, titles, and bodies; kind='term', keys and definitions. Empty lists every subject of the kind.

name: atlas_orient

data.description: candidates, ranked. A Node candidate has id, hook, and disclosure ('full', or 'roadmap' with its title); a Decision or term candidate has id, which is its atlas_read address, and hook. A related Node also has via: seed id, reference direction relative to that seed, and the source Section address.

title: Search Atlas Nodes, Decisions, and Terms
